title: Session fidelity index & probe API — personal notebook
content:
Context / motivation:
This is a lightweight personal sketch for a small client-facing probe API that returns a compact "session fidelity index" (SFI) to help the runtime and client decide: prewarm intensity, KV-prefetch budget, model variant selection, and routing priority. The goal is a cheap, privacy-conscious probe that is expressive enough for routing/economics decisions but small enough to run frequently from constrained clients.

Primary use-cases:
- Client sends an SFI probe before a burst of interactive requests to choose between fast-but-costly hot path vs cheap-cold path.
- Router uses SFI + SLA to select model variant or region.
- Telemetry: track session degradation over time (SFI trend) and trigger background rewarm/refresh.

Design principles (rough):
- Minimal wire: scalar (0-100) + small tag set + optional bucketed vector (3–6 dims).
- Deterministic mapping: same probe -> same SFI across runtime versions for comparability.
- Privacy-first: no PII, client-side hashing/sanitization; probes are ephemeral and rate-limited.
- Configurable sensitivity: allow clients/servers to trade off sensitivity vs cost.

API shape (first pass):
POST /v1/session/probe
Payload (client->server):
{
  "client_id": "anon:abcdef",          // optional, short opaque id
  "session_id": "s-1234",            // optional if present on client
  "probe_vector": [12, 0, 4],          // optional small integer vector (0-255)
  "sampled_features": ["recent_tools","last_token_entropy"], // short tag list
  "privacy_budget_token": "pb-..",    // optional one-time token for opt-in telemetry
  "ttl_hint_sec": 120                   // how long the client expects this SFI to be valid
}
Response (server->client):
{
  "sfi": 72,                            // 0-100 integer, higher = more complete/fresh
  "confidence": 0.88,                  // float (0-1), how sure we are about this score
  "variant_hint": "v2-small",        // string hint for model variant to prefer
  "prefetch_budget": 150,              // token budget client can prefetch (heuristic)
  "expiry_unix": 1700000000,           // server-side expiry for this probe
  "meta_tags": ["kv-warm-mostly","vocab-stable"]
}

Notes on fields:
- sfi: primary scalar used by routing. Computed from probe_vector + internal signals + recent telemetry. Should be stable for identical inputs across short windows.
- confidence: used by clients to choose aggressive vs conservative actions. If low, client may re-probe or fall back to safe defaults.
- prefetch_budget: units are token-equivalents (approx). Useful for client budgeting.

Compact probe vector encoding idea: pack 3–6 features into bytes to make single small base64 blob for low-bandwidth clients. Example features: 
- recent_message_count_bucket (0..7)
- avg_token_entropy_bucket (0..7)
- kv_cache_hits_bucket (0..7)
This is backwards-compatible: server interprets missing/short vectors as unknowns.

Server-side heuristics (initial):
- Start with simple linear model: sfi = clamp(w1*msg_count + w2*kv_hits + w3*entropy_inv + bias).
- Combine with real-time routing load signal: penalize SFI if target region is currently saturated.
- Apply decay: older probes get lower effective SFI over time (use ttl_hint and expiry).

Privacy & retention:
- Default: probes are not stored beyond 5 minutes, except when client supplies explicit privacy_budget_token for aggregation.
- Any stored aggregates must be irreversibly-bucketed (k-anonymized) and surfaced only as telemetry, not tied back to client_id.
- Avoid sending text or persistent identifiers. Encourage client-side feature extraction (client computes buckets).

Client SDK ergonomics (sketch):
- ProbeManager.probe(sessionId?, options?) -> Promise<{sfi, confidence, prefetchBudget}>
- Options: {forceFresh: bool, lowPriority: bool, allowTelemetry: bool}
- Automatic re-probe jittered if current sfi < threshold and user is starting an interactive flow.

ASCII diagram (rough):
client -> /v1/session/probe -> probe-gateway -> sfi-service (models/heuristics) -> routing/advisor
                          |-> telemetry-agg (opt-in only)

Edge cases & failure modes:
- network errors: fallback to client-local heuristic (simple moving avg)
- server overloaded: respond with SFI=-1 (unknown) and conservative prefetch_budget=0
- stale session_id: server returns small sfi and guidance to re-auth/restart session

Operational metrics to track:
- probe rps, p99 latency
- distribution of sfi values by region/model variant
- correlation between sfi and end-to-end latency/cost per session

Open questions / TODOs (my notes):
- Should SFI be deterministic across runtime versions? If we change model/weights, historical comparisons break but new heuristics may be better. Maybe encode "schema_version" with score to allow interpretation.
- How to best represent multi-dimensional needs (sfi scalar loses nuance). Consider returning a 3-d vector (latency_sensitivity, coherency_need, cost_sensitivity) instead of one number.
- Do we allow clients to request a bulk probe for N sessions in one call? (useful for orchestration consoles)
- Explore differential privacy for aggregated telemetry (Laplace/DP mechanisms) — JIRA-INF-3421 tracks this.
- Back-compat for on-prem/private deployments: allow an offline-only scoring module in SDK.

Quick experiments to run:
- A/B test: scalar SFI vs small vector (3 dims) for routing quality (match user-perceived latency).
- Synthetic: build simulator that generates probe vectors from conversational traces and evaluate prefetch ROI at different SFI thresholds.

Short-term plan (next 6 weeks):
1) Create minimal probe endpoint behind feature flag (only internal can call).
2) Add client SDK shim in js-sdk (opt-in).
3) Run smoke experiments with internal apps to collect SFI correlations.
4) Iterate on schema (scalar vs vector) based on telemetry.

Notes to self: keep this doc informal. Put any formal API contract into /shared_drives/product/console-and-rollouts when we have consensus. Link the experiment results to the PR above.

References / links I keep wanting to check:
- GH PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/812  (infra probe-gateway changes)
- Slack thread: #runtime-probes, thread ts=170242... (search for "sfi")
- JIRA-INF-3421: privacy + telemetry for probe APIs

End of notebook.

Unresolved (short):
- schema_version in response? (v0, v1)
- how to incentivize client SDK adoption without breaking pre-existing clients
